title: wt status --json
description: What wt up would start on, from local state alone. Printed by `wt status [<work>] --json`, which writes nothing to any repository. Schema 1: fields may be added and enumerations may gain values; nothing is renamed or removed. See docs/json.md.

schema.description: The major version: a new one only for a change that breaks readers.

schemaVersion.description: The full semantic version of this schema that the output follows: minor for an added field or enumeration value, patch for wording.

token.description: Names the inputs of this plan (trunk name, wt configuration, stack, and since 1.6.0 the remote commit of each stack member that has diverged from its own remote); pass it to `wt up --expect`. Null when not eligible, except that since 1.6.0 a plan held back by ownRemoteDiverged alone has one, for `wt up --allow-diverged --expect`.

trunk.description: Trunk as wt up resolves it here.

trunkSource.description: How trunk was determined, first match wins, from local refs alone (since 1.4.0): config — MAIN_BRANCH in the wt configuration file; originHead — refs/remotes/origin/HEAD; conventional — the first of development, main, master that exists locally or on origin (since 1.4.1; before, main, master, trunk, development, develop, ranked by where each exists); currentBranchGuess — no longer produced since 1.4.1: when nothing names trunk, detection fails and the repository reports noConfiguration. Null when trunk is.

trunkRef.description: origin/<trunk>, what wt up rebases onto after its fetch.

trunkRefUpdatedAt.description: When the trunk ref last moved, from its own reflog; null without one.

trunkSync.description: What wt up would do to local trunk after its fetch, judged against trunkTip; fastForwarded is always false here.

configured.description: A wt configuration file that parses. Since 1.3.0, false also for a repository with no file, which runs on detected defaults (what `wt init --yes` would write) with no problem named; before, that repository had no configuration at all.

worktree.description: The worktree named; null when it cannot be found.

upEligible.description: wt up would start on it. Dirt, conflicts and busy sessions are not checked here, except where they stop a fast-forward (ownRemoteBehind).

oneOf.description: Since 1.6.0 ownRemoteBehind: a member of the stack is behind its own remote and cannot be fast-forwarded (its ownRemote.blocks says why). ownRemoteDiverged: no member is, and one has diverged from its own remote; wt up --allow-diverged goes on.

upIneligibleReason.description: The code as a sentence. noConfiguration is, since 1.3.0, a repository with no file and no trunk to detect either; since 1.4.1 also a file with no MAIN_BRANCH when no trunk can be detected.

stack.description: Every worktree wt up would move, parents first.

sessionsError.description: Listing the sessions failed; sessions is then empty, not known empty.

trunkSync.description: Local trunk against origin/<trunk>, and what was done about it. See docs/json.md.

local.description: Local trunk after the run (as found unless fast-forwarded); null when there is none.

remote.description: The origin/<trunk> commit compared with; null when there is none.

localAhead.description: Commits local trunk has that origin lacks, as found.

remoteAhead.description: Commits origin has that local trunk lacks, as found.

skippedReason.description: Why local trunk was left; null when fast-forwarded or with nothing to do.

work.description: The work name, as wt list prints it.

deferredDeclared.description: Since 1.7.0. The deferred steps .wt-sync.yaml declares on trunkTip, trunk as last fetched, in the declared order: what wt up goes through once it has rebased this member. Declared, not predicted: each may run. A step with no paths does, after every finished rebase; one with paths only when the rebase changed one of them; none after a step that failed. wt up fetches first and reads the declaration from the trunk it then rebases onto, which may be newer, and the token does not cover it. The same list on every member. Empty when trunk declares none or has no .wt-sync.yaml, when trunkRefExists is false, and when the declaration there cannot be read.

declaredStep.description: One deferred step .wt-sync.yaml on trunk declares under defer:, before any rebase. See docs/json.md.

step.description: Its run line: the string deferred[].step carries for it in wt sync rebase --json.

paths.description: The globs that gate it, as declared. Empty: it runs after every finished rebase. Otherwise it runs only when the rebase changed a path one of them matches, which is not known before the rebase.

ownRemote.description: Since 1.6.0: a branch against its own remote, the remote-tracking ref a push of it would replace: what is recorded for the branch (branch.<name>.wtPushTo), else the branch's own name on the remote git pushes it to (refs/remotes/origin/<branch> unless <branch>@{push} has that name on another remote, or branch.<name>.pushRemote or remote.pushDefault names one). Since 1.8.0 never a branch of another name that is not recorded, whatever <branch>@{push} is. Never the upstream as such: a branch cut from trunk often tracks trunk and pushes to its own name. See docs/json.md.

ref.description: The remote-tracking ref, as remote/branch (origin/feat/x); null only when no ref could be named: for none, and for unknown unless it is a ref that could not be compared.

state.description: none: nothing to check: the ref is trunk's, or does not exist. gone: the branch names a ref the remote no longer has. unknown: where a push lands cannot be read from a tracking ref (a mirror remote, several push URLs, a push URL that is another repository than the fetch URL), or the branches or the remotes cannot be read at all, or the two tips cannot be compared; a run goes on unchecked. Since 1.8.0 also a branch a run would rebase and not push: noPushReason is then non-null. inSync: the same commit. ahead: only the branch has commits of its own. behind: only the remote has; a run fast-forwards the branch first. rebased: both have, and the remote's are old versions of the branch's (its tip is a tip the branch once had, or every commit only it has is matched patch for patch); a run goes on. diverged: both have, otherwise; a run refuses unless --allow-diverged.

commit.description: The remote commit compared with; null for none, gone and unknown.

ahead.description: Commits only the branch has; null for none, gone and unknown.

behind.description: Commits only the remote has; null for none, gone and unknown.

fetched.description: Always false here: wt status does not fetch, so the remote side is as last fetched.

blocks.description: Why a run would refuse for it; non-null only when a run would. diverged with state diverged, for a branch a run would rebase: --allow-diverged goes on. operation, dirty, session with state behind: it cannot be fast-forwarded, because a git operation is in progress there, the checkout has tracked changes, or an agent session is busy in it.

noPushReason.description: Since 1.8.0: why a run would rebase the branch and not push it, in words; null when a run would push it, and for state none. It tracks a remote branch of another name and nothing is recorded for it (state unknown, fixCommand settles it); what is recorded for it cannot be used (state unknown); or it is recorded as pushing to a branch of another name that has commits it never had, is at a commit it was never at, or cannot be compared with it (state diverged, behind, rebased or unknown). See docs/json.md.

fixCommand.description: Since 1.8.0: the command that settles noPushReason, as an argv, when one does: wt sync push-to <branch> <remote>/<branch>, which records the branch it tracks as where it pushes. The same command with the branch's own name on the remote records that instead. It names no directory: run it in the repository. Null otherwise.

kind.description: Since 1.5.0 also codex: a Codex session. name is then codex, codex exec, or codex (<originator>) for a thread an app-server runs.
